paragraphs.text: Screen frames and log lines on one millisecond timeline for DeepSeek Harness: record, mark, box, and
hand your agent a keyframe strip + GIF + aligned log slice.
# Incident Studio · dsh-incident-studio
English | 中文
A right-sidebar plugin for DeepSeek Harness that **puts screen frames, log lines and keyboard/mouse
input on one millisecond timeline**. Record, mark the seconds that went wrong, drag boxes on the fra
me, type one sentence — then hand the agent a keyframe strip, an animated GIF, the aligned log slice
and your description, straight into the composer.
Nothing here is game- or project-specific: log sources are configured, any program that writes a fil
e works, programs can push events directly, and the input recorder is told which process to watch.
## The problem it solves
A hands-on bug report ("I picked up the chest and the character floats") is obvious **on screen** an
d obscure **in the log**. You write a sentence, the agent has to guess which of the last 900 log lin
es was "that moment" — and which key you happened to press.
This plugin ties four things to one clock:
| Evidence | Where it comes from | Precision |
| Picture | Host-side frame capture (three paths, below) | 6 fps by default, every frame carries wal

l-clock time |
| Events | Log file tailing, markers, HTTP ingest | line-write time, tens of ms; inge

st can be exact |
| Keys/mouse | Polling helper, only while a target owns the foreground | ~30 Hz, ±

1 sample |
| Your words | boxes drawn on the frame + one sentence | attached to the selected range |
Every delivered log line is prefixed with `[00:12.340]` relative to the recording start — the same o
rigin as the frames and the key events — so the agent never has to guess the moment, or what you pre
as the frames and the key events — so the agent never has to guess the moment, or what you pressed.
## What you get on disk
Into **the current session workspace**, `.dsh-incidents/<recording-id>/`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
An excerpt of `bundle.md`:

[代码示例省略，未执行]
log
[00:12.210] (host) RConnectGame: moveTest -> 966,900
[00:14.250] (host) ReferenceEr

ror: chest state mismatch (sost:LEVITATING)
[00:15.000] ⚑ problem
[代码示例省略，未执行]
What lands in the composer is the **compact** version: phenomenon, range, artifact paths, box notes,
the key/mouse counts, and at most 80 log lines (errors and markers kept first, marks carry their "l
ast input"); the full record is one path away.
## Privacy and boundaries
- **Frames are captured only after you press Start recording, and stop when you stop.** The GDI path

grabs the whole virtual desktop — move sensitive windows away first.
- **Key/mouse recording runs o
nly during a recording and, by default, only while a target process is in front.** It records *which
key went down/up and where the mouse clicked* — **no text at all** (no layout translation, no `ToUn
icode`) — and installs no keyboard hooks. The plugin host process is always excluded, so typing into

the panel or the chat is never recorded.
- Frames, GIFs, the raw key/mouse record and the note are
written **only** into the session workspace's `.dsh-incidents/`; `profiles.json` and the three recei
pts (`client-boot.json`, `capture-capability.json`, `input-capability.json`) live in `$DSH_HOME/stor
ages/dsh-incident-studio/`. The recorder's temporary JSONL lives in the system temp folder and is de

leted right after being archived into the incident folder.
- **No network calls, no telemetry.** Dat
a reaches a model only after you press Fill composer / Send — through DSH's normal message path, exa

ctly like typing it yourself.
- Every `/dsh-incident-studio/api/*` route goes through the host's sam
e-origin check; other local processes can only push events with the per-process `x-incident-token`.

`/open` may only open paths inside this session's `.dsh-incidents/`.
- The self-check receipts recor
d counts and stages only (`client-boot.json`: how far the page got; `capture-capability.json`: how m
any screens/windows exist; `input-capability.json`: key-table size and timing). No window titles, no
pixels, no keystrokes.
## Known limitations
- **Publishing timing**: the host half is assembled at boot (editing `index.js` needs a DSH restart)
; the browser bundle follows live updates and re-runs `apply` when the host republishes. Measured: a
**real content change** to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` triggers a host recompose, editing file

s inside the plugin folder does not.
- **Alignment precision**: tailing sees a line once it is writt

en, so expect tens of milliseconds; use `/ingest` with `wall` when it must be exact.
- **The desktop
path is a frame sequence, not a video**: 6 fps reads gradient/interpolation glitches fine, single-f

rame animation curves less so. Raising `captureFps` to 10–15 costs memory and JPEG work.
- **GDI gra

bs the whole desktop**: no per-window capture, all monitors merged.
- **GIF uses one 128-colour pale
tte** (fixed from the first frame): small files and a clean picture for screen content; large gradie

nts may band slightly.
- **Browser webm extraction relies on seeking**: `MediaRecorder` output has n

o index, so a trailing frame can be lost in extreme cases.
- **No voice**: descriptions are typed an

d boxed.
- **Input is recorded only while a target owns the foreground** — that is a safety default,

not a defect. Use `scope: "all"` to widen it, at the cost of recording other windows' keys too.
- *
*No mouse wheel**: `GetAsyncKeyState` cannot see wheel deltas; that would need a mouse hook or Raw I

nput, which this plugin deliberately avoids. Mark and describe wheel actions instead.
- **Input timi

ng is ±1 sample**: 20 ms (~30 Hz) by default, `pollMs: 10` for ~60 Hz (slightly more CPU).
- **The h
elper needs to compile C#**: antivirus/EDR may block runtime compilation and loading of the small as
sembly (hit exactly that on the development machine: `Add-Type`'s temp file was refused). That is wh
y the plugin runs a real probe at start-up, writes `input-capability.json`, and shows the reason in

Settings; when blocked, only input recording is unavailable.
- **Artifacts live in the workspace**:
add `.dsh-incidents/` to your `.gitignore` (that includes `input.jsonl`).
